item.title: NMS Capital launches specialty MGA, Ascendra
item.dc:creator: Kane Wells
item.description:
Private equity firm NMS Capital Group has launched Ascendra Specialty Inc., a technology-driven, full-service managing general agency and program manager. The new MGA reportedly specialises in bespoke insurance programmes across defined market segments, providing underwriting expertise, delegated authority and claims stewardship on behalf of its carrier partners. NMS said Ascendra’s launch builds on its insurance-sector […]

The post NMS Capital launches specialty MGA, Ascendra appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
Private equity firm NMS Capital Group has launched Ascendra Specialty Inc., a technology-driven, full-service managing general agency and program manager.

The new MGA reportedly specialises in bespoke insurance programmes across defined market segments, providing underwriting expertise, delegated authority and claims stewardship on behalf of its carrier partners.

NMS said Ascendra’s launch builds on its insurance-sector strategy of developing dedicated platforms to deploy capital across targeted segments of the insurance and reinsurance markets.

According to the firm, Ascendra will initially focus on approximately eight dedicated business lines ranging from Professional Liability, Workers Comp, Transportation, Cyber, Construction, Property, Environmental and Small Business/Specialty.

As part of the launch, Ascendra has partnered with Moonshot Foundry Inc., leveraging its proprietary technology platform and carrier and retail agency network.

Trevor M. Saliba, Founder, Chairman & CEO of NMS, commented, “We are pleased to formally announce the launch of Ascendra Specialty following extensive market and sector research.

“We are equally excited to partner with Moonshot as both a capital, technology and strategic partner leveraging their proprietary technology platform and deep industry and operational resources as a leader in the insurance sector.”

Jeff Brown, CEO of Moonshot, said, “Trevor and his talented team are ideal partners for Moonshot’s accelerated launch program. Our Sherpa team is working side by side with Ascendra to accelerate their launch, connecting them with the full strength of Moonshot’s ecosystem, from our AI-enabled platform and digital distribution capabilities to operational support, innovative financing, and captive management solutions.”

The post NMS Capital launches specialty MGA, Ascendra appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.

item.title: Ariel Re adds Tamsin Webster as Chief People Officer
item.dc:creator: Saumya Jain
item.description:
Ariel Re, a global reinsurance business, has appointed Tamsin Webster as Chief People Officer. Most recently, she served at ECI Partners as Head of People, establishing the firm’s first internal HR function and strengthening its leadership succession planning. Webster has over two decades of experience in global human resources leadership across financial services, technology and […]

The post Ariel Re adds Tamsin Webster as Chief People Officer appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
Ariel Re, a global reinsurance business, has appointed Tamsin Webster as Chief People Officer.

Most recently, she served at ECI Partners as Head of People, establishing the firm’s first internal HR function and strengthening its leadership succession planning.

Webster has over two decades of experience in global human resources leadership across financial services, technology and private equity-backed businesses.

In the past, she has served as the Chief People Officer at Fulcrum Asset Management, and led the expansion of the people function to support the firm’s growth.

In the past, Webster has held senior HR leadership roles at UBS, BlackRock, and Lloyds Banking Group, alongside advising high-growth businesses on leadership, organisational design and culture.

Ryan Mather, Chief Executive Officer, Ariel Re, commented, “We are delighted to welcome Tamsin to Ariel Re. Her extensive experience across global organisations and high-growth businesses brings a valuable perspective to our leadership team.

“As we continue to grow, her expertise in talent development will be instrumental in strengthening our position as an academy firm, where the best in the business want to work, learn and develop.”

Webster added, “I am incredibly excited to join Ariel Re as Chief People Officer. From my first meetings with Ryan and the team, I was inspired by the entrepreneurial spirit, ambition and drive for excellence.

“I look forward to bringing my experience to the team and playing a part in Ariel Re’s next chapter of growth.”

The post Ariel Re adds Tamsin Webster as Chief People Officer appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.

item.title: W. R. Berkley’s Q3’26 GWP rise to $3.95bn
item.dc:creator: Saumya Jain
item.description:
Insurance holding company W. R. Berkley Corporation reported gross written premiums (GWP) of $3.95 billion for the third quarter of 2026, up from $3.83 billion in Q3’25. For the first nine months of 2026, GWP were reported at $11.9 billion, compared to $11.5 billion in 9M’25. The firm’s insurance segment was the largest contributor to […]

The post W. R. Berkley’s Q3’26 GWP rise to $3.95bn appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
Insurance holding company W. R. Berkley Corporation reported gross written premiums (GWP) of $3.95 billion for the third quarter of 2026, up from $3.83 billion in Q3’25. For the first nine months of 2026, GWP were reported at $11.9 billion, compared to $11.5 billion in 9M’25.

The firm’s insurance segment was the largest contributor to GWP, generating $3.6 billion in Q3’26, a growth of 4.9% and $10.7 billion in 9M’26, a 3.2% rise.

Meanwhile, the reinsurance segment generated Q3’26 GWP of $391 million and $443 million for 9M’26.

Additionally, the insurer confirmed that for the quarter, its insurance segment’s pre-tax underwriting income rose by 10.6% to $237.7 million.

Overall, net written premiums (NWP) remained broadly increased year over year, reaching $3.3 billion for Q3’26, compared to $3.2 billion in Q3’25. For 9M’26, NWP were $9.9 billion, compared to $9.7 billion in 9M’25.

The insurer reported net premiums earned (NPE) of $3.21 billion for Q3’26, compared to $3.15 billion in the comparative quarter; for 9M1’26, NPE was $9.5 billion, compared to $9.3 billion in 9M’25.

Meanwhile, the quarter’s current accident year combined ratio before catastrophe losses of 2.7 loss ratio points was 88.1%, while the reported combined ratio was 90.8%.

Across all lines of business, catastrophe losses rose slightly to $85.9 million for Q3’26, compared to $78.5 million in Q3’25. At the same time, catastrophe losses for 9M’26 were down to $223 million, compared to $288 million in 9M’25.

For Q3’26, net income dropped to $446 million compared to $511 million in Q3’25; for 9M’26, it rose to $1.4 billion compared to $1.3 billion for 9M’25.

The operating income for this quarter rose by 6.4% to $456 million compared to $440 million in Q3’25. For 9M’26, it was $1.5 billion, compared to $1.3 billion at 9M’25.

Meanwhile, Q2’26 net investment income grew to $383.5 million for the quarter, driven by an increase in the core portfolio of 12%, compared to $351 million in Q3’25. For 9M’26, it was  $1.2 billion, compared to $1 billion for 9M’25.

W. Robert Berkley, Jr., Chairman, Chief Executive Officer, and President, W. R. Berkley Corporation, commented, “The Company delivered another excellent quarter, generating an annualized 18.8% operating return on beginning-of-year stockholders’ equity. These results demonstrate the continuing strength in how we manage our specialty insurance underwriting, as well as our investment portfolio.

“Our underwriting results have consistently been outstanding due to our unwavering commitment to rate adequacy and attention to terms and conditions. As the cycles for various product lines have decoupled, the breadth of our offering through our 60 specialty businesses allows for greater stability. Our long-term view and disciplined approach produced a strong 88.1% accident year combined ratio, excluding catastrophe losses.”

He continued, “Our investment portfolio continues to be a great contributor to our economic model, with the domestic fixed-maturity portfolio serving as the primary driver. Income from fixed-maturity securities increased 10.3% over the corresponding period a year ago. The credit quality of our portfolio remains excellent, with an average strong AA- rating, and reinvestment yields continue to meaningfully exceed our portfolio’s book yield.

“Our disciplined approach to capital management remains unchanged. We returned a total of $728.6 million to shareholders year-to-date, which includes $435.1 million of share repurchases, while preserving substantial flexibility to support future opportunities.

“The strong prevailing interest rate tailwind has set investment income on a path to greater earnings contributions, and greater utilization of technology is enabling us to further leverage our underwriting and claims expertise. We believe we remain well-positioned to continue delivering attractive long-term risk-adjusted returns and creating long-term value for our shareholders.”

The post W. R. Berkley’s Q3’26 GWP rise to $3.95bn appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.

item.dc:creator: Saumya Jain
item.description:
Matthew Dragonetti, President of Arch Reinsurance Group, part of Bermuda-based Arch Capital Group Ltd., will retire effective March 2027, after spending 25 years with the reinsurer. Dragonetti joined Arch Re in 2001 as one of the first employees, serving as a Senior US Property Treaty Underwriter. He subsequently held several leadership positions of increasing responsibility, […]

The post Arch Re’s Matthew Dragonetti to retire in Q1’27 after 25 years appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
Matthew Dragonetti, President of Arch Reinsurance Group, part of Bermuda-based Arch Capital Group Ltd., will retire effective March 2027, after spending 25 years with the reinsurer.

Dragonetti joined Arch Re in 2001 as one of the first employees, serving as a Senior US Property Treaty Underwriter.

He subsequently held several leadership positions of increasing responsibility, leading to his current role as President and Chief Commercial Officer.

In the past, Dragonetti has also served as the President and Head of Property, Head of Worldwide Property, and Head of US Property.

Jerome Halgan, Chief Executive Officer, Arch Global Reinsurance Group, commented, “Matt has been an important part of Arch’s success over the past 25 years, and we are incredibly grateful for his leadership and contributions.

“He embodies our culture and has been relentless in helping Arch Re on its commitment to consistently deliver meaningful value to its clients. Matt will be dearly missed. We wish him the best and are happy his retirement will allow him to spend more time with his family.”

Dragonetti added, “I’m tremendously proud of all that we have accomplished together. It has been a privilege to work alongside such talented colleagues and to help build the business over the past 25 years.

“I’m grateful for the relationships I’ve developed throughout my time at Arch and have every confidence in the team’s continued success.”

The post Arch Re’s Matthew Dragonetti to retire in Q1’27 after 25 years appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.

item.title: Reinsurers must focus on cedent needs to attract more inflow: Gallagher Re’s Deschars
item.dc:creator: Kassandra Jimenez-Sanchez
item.description:
Reinsurance capital providers that have the best listening capability and the strongest appetite for creative problem-solving will see the most cedents “knocking at their door” as they rethink their reinsurance strategies in this soft market, according to Gallagher Re’s Ditte Deschars. In a recent interview with Reinsurance News ahead of the annual Baden-Baden reinsurance symposium, […]

The post Reinsurers must focus on cedent needs to attract more inflow: Gallagher Re’s Deschars appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
Reinsurance capital providers that have the best listening capability and the strongest appetite for creative problem-solving will see the most cedents “knocking at their door” as they rethink their reinsurance strategies in this soft market, according to Gallagher Re’s Ditte Deschars.

In a recent interview with Reinsurance News ahead of the annual Baden-Baden reinsurance symposium, Gallagher Re’s EMEA Chair, Deschars, highlighted empathy and client engagement as key differentiators in this competitive and evolving landscape.

The executive stated: “For any capital to be relevant, reinsurers should be empathetic, they must have a strong listening approach, listen to what the clients need and then really think about how they can help with that, within their own risk appetite framework, so that it works for both parties.

“Capital providers that have the best listening capability, and look to find solutions, will see that many cedents will knock on their door.”

Cedents are being advised to capitalise on the abundant supply of capital and softening market conditions, but not only to chase quick discounts, but to restructure their broader reinsurance purchasing for longer-term resilience.

While buyers in a softening market frequently prioritise reductions and short-term financial gain to meet certain KPIs, Deschars cautioned that doing so risks missing a prime strategic window.

“The cycle that we’re in will allow clients, of course, to have some cost benefits,” Deschars observed. “But they can do so much more with their buying, they can reconsider appropriate retention levels and the breadth of coverage, and not just the terms but also the conditions of the coverage.”

Adding: “We are advising clients to take full use of the current market cycle, to reconsider the scope to be even better aligned with client’s long-term objectives and to really create longer term value. If you don’t do it now, you might miss a good opportunity, as you never know what is going to happen next year. So, think about your objectives longer term and shape your programme to fit that strategy.”

Unlike previous market cycles triggered by distress or rapid capital degradation, the current softening phase is unfolding from a position of exceptional balance-sheet strength, Deschars noted.

She said: “The market has been softening for a while, but it is softening from an incredibly strong financial basis. Reinsurers have had great profitability; the returns are well above cost of capital. We see that the capital is continuing to build up because of the retained earnings, and this is despite higher dividend payouts, despite reserve strengthening.”

The executive added that Gallagher Re expects these healthy returns to carry forward into 2027, providing a stable foundation for cedents and reinsurers to build sustainable partnerships.

A critical element of the current market dynamic is the structural expansion of capital providers, spanning both traditional and alternative balance sheets.

“More buyers are seeing the many different sources of capital available that are attracted by different sets of risk profiles, and returns,” Deschars noted. “There isn’t just one innovative capital structure that will create the best value. It’s actually more about what is now happening across the broader platform of both traditional and alternative capital. And that whole platform can now serve as a much more easily available interlinked capital ecosystem for clients to take advantage of.”

“What has happened now is that we have an enlargement in the supply, which is much more flexible and open to deploy the capital to different types of risk profiles, to different types of margin matrices, etc. So, what we see today is that a much larger part of our client segment will have this whole capital ecosystem available to them, which they didn’t have a few years ago,” she added.

With capital expanding across traditional reinsurers and alternative markets, Deschars advises to focus more on sustainable reinsurance partnerships rather than commoditised capacity.

By leveraging this diverse ecosystem, cedents and reinsurers can move on to build resilient structures that optimise retentions and hold firm through market cycles.

The post Reinsurers must focus on cedent needs to attract more inflow: Gallagher Re’s Deschars appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.

In his new position, Cushway will work to help broaden Chaucer’s UK P&C offering and enhance its ability to deliver specialist solutions across the country, supporting Chaucer’s ambition to build […]

The post Cushway to lead Chaucer’s UK P&C team appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
Global specialty re/insurance group Chaucer has expanded its UK capabilities with the appointment of Ryan Cushway as Head of UK Property & Casualty, effective immediately.

In his new position, Cushway will work to help broaden Chaucer’s UK P&C offering and enhance its ability to deliver specialist solutions across the country, supporting Chaucer’s ambition to build a leading UK P&C proposition.

An experienced executive with deep underwriting expertise, extensive market knowledge and well-established broker relationships, Cushway is joining Chaucer from Sompo, where he served as Head of International & UK Casualty.

Prior to this, he held several senior positions at Aspen in similar classes of business, with earlier experience at Liberty Specialty Markets.

Paul Restarick, Head of Non-Marine Insurance at Chaucer, said: “We are delighted to welcome Ryan to Chaucer. He brings a wealth of experience, a strong track record of underwriting performance and deep broker relationships that will further strengthen our position in the UK market.

“This appointment represents a significant investment in our Property & Casualty capabilities and demonstrates our commitment to building a market-leading proposition for brokers and clients. The combination of Ryan’s leadership, expertise, and the scale of capacity we are deploying creates an exciting platform for future growth.”

Cushway added: “I am thrilled to be joining Chaucer at such an exciting stage in its development. Chaucer has built a strong reputation for underwriting excellence, long-term partnerships and empowering talented teams to succeed.

“We look forward to establishing a leading UK Property & Casualty offering, delivering outstanding service to brokers and clients, and building a business that can grow sustainably over the years ahead.”

 

The post Cushway to lead Chaucer’s UK P&C team appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.

item.title: Moody’s forecasts further growth in German insurers’ private credit investments
item.dc:creator: Taylor Mixides
item.description:
German insurers are expected to increase their investment in private credit as they seek higher returns, diversify portfolios and match assets with long-term policyholder liabilities, according to Moody’s Ratings, the international credit rating agency. In a new report, the agency explained that it expects these investments to create additional challenges around asset valuation, liquidity and […]

The post Moody’s forecasts further growth in German insurers’ private credit investments appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
German insurers are expected to increase their investment in private credit as they seek higher returns, diversify portfolios and match assets with long-term policyholder liabilities, according to Moody’s Ratings, the international credit rating agency.

In a new report, the agency explained that it expects these investments to create additional challenges around asset valuation, liquidity and risk management, potentially prompting greater regulatory scrutiny.

However, the agency does not anticipate a material weakening of German insurers’ credit profiles, citing their established investment strategies, generally stable liabilities, strong asset-liability management and robust capital positions.

German insurers have steadily increased their exposure to illiquid investments over the past decade, partly in response to the low interest rate environment that ended in 2022. According to Moody’s, these assets can offer additional returns, portfolio diversification and predictable cash flows that help insurers meet long-term financial commitments.

Based on data from the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA), Moody’s estimates that illiquid assets accounted for 19.4% of German insurers’ invested assets in 2025, compared with 15.8% in 2019. Among life insurers, the proportion increased from 19% to 25.1%, reflecting demand for investments capable of supporting savings products with guaranteed returns.

Mortgages and loans remain the largest category of illiquid investments, although allocations to private equity, infrastructure and alternative funds have grown. These fund-based investments represented around 15% of German insurers’ illiquid assets in 2025, up from 5% in 2019. Moody’s cautions that the available figures may understate overall exposure because some private debt investments are recorded within broader corporate bond categories.

Private credit accounted for approximately 9.3% of German insurers’ total invested assets at the end of 2024, exceeding the European insurance sector average of 7.5%, according to Moody’s Ratings. Germany, France and the Netherlands together represented around 72% of European insurers’ combined private credit exposure, with Germany accounting for roughly half of that total.

The agency says German insurers’ exposure is concentrated in established investment categories, particularly mortgages, loans and privately placed corporate debt. Mortgages and loans, including holdings through funds, accounted for around 71% of private credit investments, supported by their predictable cash flows and suitability for matching long-term liabilities.

Unlisted or untraded corporate bonds represented a further 21% of German insurers’ private credit portfolios. These holdings totalled €92 billion at the end of 2024, equivalent to approximately 60% of the wider European insurance industry’s exposure to the same category.

Moody’s attributes Germany’s comparatively high allocation partly to the longstanding use of private placement instruments, including Schuldscheindarlehen (SSD), or promissory notes, and Namensschuldverschreibungen (NSV), registered debt instruments issued to named investors. These instruments offer insurers opportunities to diversify credit exposure and improve returns, although they generally have limited secondary-market liquidity.

The agency considers these established investments less risky than newer private credit strategies, such as middle-market lending, asset-based finance and more complex structured investments. It also notes that Solvency II capital requirements encourage insurers to consider credit quality and investment duration when selecting assets.

Moody’s expects growth in German insurers’ overall allocation to illiquid assets to moderate in the near term as higher interest rates improve the relative attractiveness of publicly traded fixed-income investments. The German 10-year government bond yield reached approximately 3.5% at the beginning of October 2026, its highest level in a decade, according to the agency.

Higher borrowing costs have also affected property valuations and private equity returns. Weak economic growth in Germany has weighed on property transactions, while limited private equity exit activity has delayed distributions to investors and increased liquidity considerations. Some insurers have responded by limiting new commitments or reducing target allocations in certain asset classes.

Nevertheless, Moody’s expects private credit exposure to continue growing, potentially at a faster rate than insurers’ overall illiquid asset holdings. Growth in traditional life insurance business remains subdued, limiting the scope for insurers to expand their investment portfolios overall. Moody’s therefore expects portfolio reallocation, rather than substantial growth in total invested assets, to be an important driver of increased private credit exposure.

Germany’s financing requirements could provide further opportunities for insurers to invest in infrastructure, defence, the energy transition and digitalisation. Moody’s expects private capital to play a growing role alongside public funding, with changes to the EU’s Solvency II capital framework due to take effect in 2027 potentially supporting greater investment in securitised assets.

The agency also expects German insurers to gradually broaden their private credit portfolios to include direct corporate lending, infrastructure debt and asset-based finance. Moody’s warns that increasing private credit exposure brings additional challenges because assets with limited secondary-market activity can be difficult to sell quickly during periods of financial stress. Valuations may also rely on models, external appraisals and investment manager estimates rather than observable market prices.

The agency cautions that comparatively stable reported valuations do not necessarily indicate lower underlying economic risk, as infrequent transactions can delay the recognition of changes in asset values. German accounting rules also allow many long-term debt investments to be carried at nominal value, acquisition cost or a figure similar to amortised cost, depending on the asset and its classification.

Despite these risks, Moody’s considers the likelihood of forced asset sales by German life insurers to be relatively low. Many traditional savings policies discourage early surrender, while long-term liabilities and established asset-liability management practices can help insurers retain illiquid investments during periods of market volatility.

The agency says larger German insurers generally have established capabilities in credit analysis, investment selection and risk management. However, smaller insurers and companies adopting more specialised strategies may rely more heavily on external managers, increasing the importance of manager selection, internal expertise and effective oversight.

Regulatory attention is also increasing. German financial regulator BaFin is examining risks associated with private credit, including limited transparency, interconnectedness and the demands placed on investment risk management.

Moody’s does not expect the expansion of private credit to materially weaken German insurers’ credit profiles. The agency cites their concentration in established assets with generally strong credit characteristics, long-term liabilities, effective asset-liability management and robust capitalisation as important mitigating factors. German life insurers recorded an average Solvency II coverage ratio of 374% at the end of 2025, according to Moody’s Ratings.

The post Moody’s forecasts further growth in German insurers’ private credit investments appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.

item.title: AXA XL appoints Erin Bouren as Underwriting Manager for E&S Casualty
item.dc:creator: Beth Musselwhite
item.description:
AXA XL, the property and casualty specialty risk division of AXA, has announced the appointment of Erin Bouren as Underwriting Manager for E&S Casualty in the western region of the US. In her new role, Bouren will focus on driving growth, managing the portfolio and strengthening broker relationships, supporting the ongoing expansion of AXA XL’s […]

The post AXA XL appoints Erin Bouren as Underwriting Manager for E&S Casualty appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
AXA XL, the property and casualty specialty risk division of AXA, has announced the appointment of Erin Bouren as Underwriting Manager for E&S Casualty in the western region of the US.

In her new role, Bouren will focus on driving growth, managing the portfolio and strengthening broker relationships, supporting the ongoing expansion of AXA XL’s Excess & Surplus Casualty business.

She will report to Laura Johnson, Head of West, E&S Casualty, and work alongside Cassandra Rotunno, who supports the central region.

Bouren brings more than 20 years of industry experience, with a strong background in casualty underwriting, portfolio management, business development and team leadership. She specialises in Excess & Surplus and admitted underwriting, with full P&L ownership for portfolios spanning the middle market through to large and complex risks.

She joins AXA XL from Everest Insurance, where she most recently served as West Region Leader for National Account & Middle Market Excess Casualty. In this role, she established and scaled a diversified $36 million book across the Mountain States, California, the Southwest and the Pacific Northwest, delivering consistent rates, strong retention and disciplined underwriting governance.

Before that, Bouren served as Vice President of Underwriting for the Western Region at Conifer Insurance Services. She also held leadership and underwriting roles at Ironshore, Arch and GenRe.

Johnson commented, “Erin is a highly respected underwriting professional with deep casualty expertise and established relationships throughout the western region.

“Her proven track record in building profitable portfolios, developing talent, and delivering results makes her a valuable addition to our team as we continue to grow our E&S Casualty footprint.”

The post AXA XL appoints Erin Bouren as Underwriting Manager for E&S Casualty appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.

item.title: Howden Re highlights reinsurance’s role as a capital tool as prices soften
item.dc:creator: Kane Wells
item.description:
Insurers should treat reinsurance as a capital management tool rather than simply a form of protection, according to Howden Re, which argues that a softening market presents an opportunity to reassess risk retention and improve returns. “The best performers treat reinsurance as a capital tool, not only as protection,” the broker said in a report […]

The post Howden Re highlights reinsurance’s role as a capital tool as prices soften appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
Insurers should treat reinsurance as a capital management tool rather than simply a form of protection, according to Howden Re, which argues that a softening market presents an opportunity to reassess risk retention and improve returns.

“The best performers treat reinsurance as a capital tool, not only as protection,” the broker said in a report benchmarking 42 European non-life insurers over 2023-25.

It found that the strongest performers combined good underwriting with leaner capital positions, while some insurers holding the largest solvency buffers generated relatively weak returns.

The capital-light, high-return group held around €28 of capital for every €100 of premium, compared with €86 for the capital-intensive, low-return group. The former averaged a return on equity of around 22%, while the latter returned less than 5%.

Howden Re said the current buyer-friendly reinsurance market, with prices softening, allows insurers to redesign programmes around their capital plans.

This could include reviewing retentions, transferring volatility where they lack an advantage in pricing or data, and protecting against accumulated exposures.

However, the broker stressed that capital efficiency cannot compensate for weak underwriting.

Insurers with the best combined ratios averaged around 17% return on equity, compared with around 4% for those with the weakest, while capital efficiency amplified rather than created good underwriting results.

The report urged insurers to review reinsurance structures against explicit capital and return targets rather than simply renewing existing programmes.

It also called for investment risk to be considered alongside underwriting exposures, as market risk can account for a significant part of an insurer’s capital requirements.

Howden Re cautioned that holding less capital is only beneficial if an insurer can withstand stress, noting that its analysis did not test balance-sheet resilience.

As Reinsurance News understands, the appropriate capital buffer therefore depends on how an insurer would respond to severe but plausible scenarios, rather than how its solvency ratio compares with peers.

The post Howden Re highlights reinsurance’s role as a capital tool as prices soften appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.

item.dc:creator: Kassandra Jimenez-Sanchez
item.description:

As […]

The post Femia to lead newly launched DOXA Re as President appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
DOXA, a US-based managing general underwriter (MGU) platform, has announced the formation of DOXA Re, a specialty property reinsurance MGU focused on quota share and related proportional solutions for traditional insurers, hybrid carriers and managing general agents (MGAs).

“DOXA Re addresses a growing need for specialty underwriting expertise in the quota share reinsurance marketplace. As MGA and hybrid-carrier programs expand, property placements are becoming more complex, yet access to reinsurers with both the expertise and appetite to participate remains limited,” says DOXA’s chief product and underwriting officer, Joe Guerrero.

Adding: “DOXA Re brings together experienced underwriting, analytics and DOXA’s operational resources to move quickly and thoughtfully to meet the needs of carriers and MGAs.”

James Femia will lead DOXA Re as President, bringing 22 years of property reinsurance underwriting and leadership experience to the position.

Over the course of his career, Femia has built strong partnerships with brokers, cedents, MGAs, and capital markets players while overseeing diverse quota share portfolios.

Under Femia’s leadership, DOXA Re is to establish a balanced portfolio spanning multiple risk classes, product lines, geographic regions, and client segments.

Combining delegated underwriting authority with workflows that support timely reviews and clear communication, DOXA Re aims to provide clients and brokers with continuity from initial review through binding.

Backed by DOXA’s robust operational infrastructure, the MGU will expand its team by recruiting top-tier underwriting and analytics talent committed to rigorous pricing, disciplined risk selection, and thoughtful treaty design.

Femia commented: “Our approach reflects what I call ‘Working Property’: putting capital to work alongside cedents and collaborating with brokers and capacity providers so everyone at the table shares the success.

“We want to be the first call because we know how to navigate risk, capitalize on opportunity and do what we say we will do. That is how we build lasting partnerships and a sustainable business.”

The post Femia to lead newly launched DOXA Re as President appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
